subject: Post-call: HealthSync inference unit-econ & MAP
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@healthsync.ai>, Procurement <procure@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: HealthSync inference unit-econ & MAP

Hi Sara / HealthSync team —

Thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few concrete asks so we can turn this into a mutual action plan.

High-level notes / assumptions we captured:
- Primary feature: AI-assisted intake + clinical summary generation for telehealth visits.
- Expected monthly usage (from your product PM): 70k–90k sessions/month; avg tokens per session ~1,000 (prompt + output) → ~70M–90M tokens/month.
- Target procurement budget (ballpark you mentioned): $6k–$10k / month for inference (initial pilot scope).
- Timeline: pilot starting late June; production roll by Q4 conditional on unit-econ.

Immediate asks / next steps we discussed:
1) Please confirm final monthly session estimate (70k–90k) and any seasonal spikes.
2) Confirm whether PHI will be sent to the hosted environment for the pilot — this affects Private deployment vs Dedicated and pricing.
3) We will share a conservative unit-econ workbook (attached), with model & quantization options and a split of platform fee vs infra cost. Review and flag any differing assumptions.

Preliminary unit-econ (we'll refine once you confirm volumes):
- Target $/1M tokens: you indicated procurement wants to keep inference under ~$110–$150 / 1M tokens to hit internal feature payback targets. (We'll show feasible options)
- Example baseline: 80M tokens/month @ $50 / 1M tokens → $4,000/mo inference cost (infrastructure + efficiency optimizations) + platform fee ~ $1,200/mo → ~$5,200 total.
- Cost per user action (1k tokens): ~$0.05. If feature monetizes at $1.50/month ARPU per active user, margin contribution before CAC ~ 96%; CAC payback details below in follow-up from Karthik.

Attachments included:
- HS-inference-cost-model-20270509.csv (cost assumptions + per-model estimates)
- HealthSync-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan draft with milestones & owners)

I'll follow up with a more explicit $/feature and CAC-payback table by tomorrow (Karthik will run a few model variants). Once we align on volumes and PHI handling, we'll produce a formal MAP (SOW + timeline) for procurement review.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — quick confirmations from our side:

1) Volumes: PM confirmed 80k sessions/month is the best single number to plan to for the pilot. We do expect a 30% spike during open enrollment windows (Aug–Sep) so please show sensitivity for +30%.
2) PHI: For the pilot we'll route de-identified transcripts to a hosted, encrypted endpoint (we can provide the de-id pipeline), but production likely requires Private deployment / VPC.
3) Budget: Our procurement lead shared an initial target of $7k–$9k / month for inference for pilot. That implies a target $/1M tokens roughly in the $87–$112 range given the 80M token estimate.

Please send the cost model and MAP; procurement asked that we get a draft that shows both a hosted pilot price and the delta to Private/Dedicated deployment.

Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthSync inference unit-econ & MAP

Sara — looping in the numbers Karthik (SE) running through model variants.

Assumptions used (detailed workbook attached):
- Sessions/month: 80,000 (baseline); sensitivity: 104k (baseline +30%).
- Tokens/session: 1,000 (avg). Monthly tokens: 80M (baseline) / 104M (sensitivity).
- Feature invocation pattern: 1 invocation per session.

Model/configuration scenarios (rounded):
A) Open 7B quantized (fp16 -> 4-bit quantized): infra cost ~$18 / 1M tokens; Redwood platform fee & orchestration ~$22 / 1M → total ~$40 / 1M tokens.
B) Open 13B (mixed precision): infra cost ~$36 / 1M; platform fee ~$22 → $58 / 1M.
C) LLM-hosted premium (larger vetted model + SLA): infra cost ~$85 / 1M; platform fee ~$35 → $120 / 1M.

Example economics (baseline 80M tokens):
- Scenario A: $40 / 1M => $3,200 infra+fee; platform+ops line items included in $22. Total monthly = $3,200.
- Scenario B: $58 / 1M => $4,640/mo.
- Scenario C: $120 / 1M => $9,600/mo.

Per-feature cost and margin (illustrative):
- Cost per invocation (1k tokens) = total $/1M / 1000. For scenario A = $0.04 / invocation; B = $0.058; C = $0.12.
- If you price the premium clinical summary as an add-on at $1.25 / MAU (monetized per active user), on scenario A the gross margin per monetized user is ~ (1.25 - 0.04)/1.25 ≈ 96.8%.

CAC payback (simple model):
- If acquisition cost per customer = $120, and feature drives 12 paying users on average per account with ARPU per paying user = $1.25/mo, incremental gross margin per month = 12 * (1.25 - 0.04) ≈ $14.52. CAC payback ~ 120 / 14.52 ≈ 8.3 months on scenario A.
- On scenario C (higher infra cost), payback becomes ~120 / (12*(1.25 - 0.12)) ≈ 9.7 months.

Takeaways / recommendations:
- To meet your procurement target of $7k–$9k for pilot at 80M tokens, we should aim for scenario A or B with negotiated platform fee. Scenario B sits in the middle; scenario A gives the best unit economics and clear CAC payback under 9 months.
- If PHI requires Private deployment, we will show delta pricing in the MAP (typically Private adds a one-time onboarding + higher per-M token due to isolated infra — I estimated +10–25% depending on reserved capacity).

I attached HS-inference-cost-model-20270509.csv with the line-by-line math. Happy to walk through the workbook Thursday if useful.

-karthik
